expected_segments: Higher speeds reduce the time available between seeing a problem and reaching it. On rural roads and faster routes, plan further ahead and keep enough room to change your mind.

In this chapter M06-L01 · Read the rural road M06-L02 · Is passing worth the risk? M06-L03 · Join faster traffic calmly M06-L04 · Expect an interrupted route M06-R · Review and self-assessment Answers and review guidance Official references This material is a learning aid to help you understand Swedish driving theory. It is not an official source and cannot replace official information from Trafikverket and Transportstyrelsen. Always consult their current guidance and the applicable rules.
Your goal: Identify risks from bends, crests, narrow roads, animals and slow vehicles and justify speed and position changes.

Requirements. Keep right when meeting another vehicle and leave a safe lateral gap. If an obstruction on your side prevents a safe meeting, stop if necessary to let the approaching vehicle pass. Your speed must suit the visible road and foreseeable hazards, with particular care at bends, crests and narrow meetings. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14–15 and 30

Learning approach. Read the road in sections: the visible straight, the entry to a bend, the portion hidden behind a crest and the next place someone might join. Never extend the clear section in your imagination. A vehicle emerging from a field or a cyclist beyond a bend changes what seemed to be an empty road.
Read the rural road ahead Independent examples of bends, gradients, narrowings, uneven road and passing places. Gradient numbers are percentages, not a safe-speed formula. Bends and gradients
A hazardous bend lies ahead. The symbol shows its direction; adjust speed before entering it. Left bend.
Dangerous bend. Left bend.
Continue the learning
A hazardous bend lies ahead. The symbol shows its direction; adjust speed before entering it. Right bend.
Dangerous bend. Right bend.
Several hazardous bends lie ahead. The symbol identifies the direction of the first bend. Series of bends, first to the left.
Series of dangerous bends. Series of bends, first to the left.
Several hazardous bends lie ahead. The symbol identifies the direction of the first bend. Series of bends, first to the right.
Series of dangerous bends. Series of bends, first to the right.
Continue the learning
Prepare for a steep downhill section. The number is the gradient in percent, not a speed limit. A descending slope labelled 10 percent.
Steep descent. A descending slope labelled 10 percent.
Prepare for a steep uphill section. Read the percentage as a gradient. An ascending slope labelled 10 percent.
Steep ascent. An ascending slope labelled 10 percent.
Narrow and uneven roads
Expect surface irregularities or damage that call for a lower speed. Uneven surface inside a warning triangle.
Uneven road. Uneven surface inside a warning triangle.
Continue the learning
A deliberately raised or lowered part of the road is ahead. The graphic distinguishes the form. Raised hump.
Speed-control hump or dip. Raised hump.
A deliberately raised or lowered part of the road is ahead. The graphic distinguishes the form. Dip.
Speed-control hump or dip. Dip.
A one-way carriageway changes to a carriageway carrying traffic in both directions. Opposing vertical arrows inside a warning triangle.
Two-way traffic ahead. Opposing vertical arrows inside a warning triangle.
Continue the learning
The edge may be weak or raised relative to the adjacent surface. Keep an appropriate margin. Car at a crumbling road edge inside a warning triangle.
Weak or high road edge. Car at a crumbling road edge inside a warning triangle.
This identifies a place for vehicles to pass each other on a narrow road. White M on blue.
Passing place. White M on blue.

Wild animals and reindeer can appear throughout the year. Trafikverket highlights dawn and dusk and periods of increased animal movement, but the absence of those conditions is not a guarantee. A wildlife fence can be interrupted by access points and does not remove the need to observe. Trafikverket: wildlife
Recognise animal warnings Each animal symbol has its own meaning. These examples do not imply that unpictured animals are absent.
There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Moose silhouette.
Animals ahead. Moose silhouette.
There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Deer silhouette.
Animals ahead. Deer silhouette.
There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Cattle silhouette.
Animals ahead. Cattle silhouette.

There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Horse silhouette.
Animals ahead. Horse silhouette.
There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Reindeer silhouette.
Animals ahead. Reindeer silhouette.
There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Sheep silhouette.
Animals ahead. Sheep silhouette.
Continue the learning
There is a particular risk of animals on or near the road. Read the animal symbol as part of the warning. Wild boar silhouette.
Animals ahead. Wild boar silhouette.

A slow vehicle's appearance may resemble a car even when its permitted speed and construction differ. Trafikverket advises other drivers to keep distance and pass only where appropriate. Stay far enough back to see around it and evaluate the road, rather than moving close to demand that it hurry. Slow vehicles and other traffic
Slow vehicles and following space The 50 m shown on C19 is a particular signed minimum distance, not a universal following gap for slow vehicles.
Slow-moving vehicles often cross or enter the road here. Tractor with trailer inside a warning triangle.
Slow vehicles ahead. Tractor with trailer inside a warning triangle.
Continue the learning
Keep at least the displayed distance from a motor vehicle ahead travelling in the same direction. 50 metres between two vehicle symbols.
Minimum following distance. 50 metres between two vehicle symbols.
Plan turns and read animal cues

Turn planning · Choose a safer approach. On an ordinary two-way rural road, heavy traffic may make a direct left turn unsafe. Continue to a suitable, permitted place or route where you can change direction safely, then return to approach the destination with a right turn if that movement is allowed and safe. This can avoid hazardous waiting and crossing the opposing stream at the original entrance. It is a planning alternative, not permission to turn around immediately on the carriageway. If no safe legal return route exists, choose another route or postpone. Trafikverket: example of routing to a turning place

Legal boundary. Before turning or leaving the road, protect oncoming traffic and traffic on the road you enter; take particular care of following traffic. A turnaround must cause neither danger nor obstruction. Signs and access restrictions still apply. Never turn around or reverse on a motorway or expressway. If you can wait safely and legally for a left turn, remember the advice in M04-L02 to keep the front wheels straight; that advice does not make an unsafe turn suitable. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§24, 26, 29 and 46; chapter 9 §§1–2

Worked rural alternative. A farm entrance is on your left and busy traffic leaves no safe opportunity. You continue to an accessible junction route that legally and safely brings you back in the opposite direction. The entrance is then on your right. Check people, traffic and the entrance again before turning; the revised route does not guarantee a safe final movement.

Wildlife observation · Time and terrain. Give extra attention at dawn and dusk, near animal habitats and where fences end or have openings. Scan woodland edges, bushes and small waterways beside the road: Trafikverket's road-project study describes these as animal routes that can conceal an approach. Its national guidance also describes animal passages through fence openings. These are cues for observation and speed planning, not predictions that animals only cross there. Trafikverket: wildlife and fence passages · Trafikverket: habitat example, page 9

Apply the cues. At dusk, woodland meets a field beside a gap in the fence. Read the edges and opening as possible animal approaches, and choose speed for the view and foreseeable hazard. Keep observing even on fenced stretches. Prevention belongs here; actions after a wildlife collision are in M10-L02.
Make room at the narrowing

Narrow bridge: the obstruction is on the teal driver’s right and the van approaches in its own lane. Reduce speed before the narrowing and stop if necessary. The scene does not measure a safe lateral gap.

Worked decision. You approach a narrow bridge with a van coming towards you and an obstruction on your side. You reduce speed before the narrowing and stop if necessary. Do not move into the van's path simply because you reached the obstruction first.
Check your understanding

Knowledge check. (1) No vehicle is visible beyond a crest. Is the road proved clear? (2) Heavy traffic makes your rural left turn unsafe. What alternative can you plan? (3) Which time and roadside cues call for extra wildlife attention?
Remember: Let what you can actually see determine the available space.
Your goal: Compare waiting with overtaking using visibility, speed difference, space and a safe completion path.

Requirements. Overtake only without danger and with sufficient clear road. Do not start when a following driver has begun overtaking, or pass on the left when the vehicle ahead signals an intended leftward movement. Leave safe lateral clearance and a safe return opportunity. When being overtaken, do not increase speed or otherwise make the pass harder. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§31–38

The normal passing side is left. Exceptions include a vehicle turning or clearly preparing to turn left, and the specified rules for marked same-direction lanes on roads limited to 70 km/h or less. Passing in queues or destination lanes has separate provisions; it does not remove the need to protect people at crossings. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§7, 31 and 41–42

Restrictions to recognise. Overtaking is generally prohibited immediately before or in a road junction, with specified exceptions for right-side overtaking, police/signal control, or an established yielding/stopping duty on the crossing road. Similar restrictions apply at level crossings, with exceptions for barriers or road-junction-type traffic signals. At an obscured bend or crest, do not use an opposing lane to overtake; the detailed provision contains limited exceptions. Section 39 also contains an exception for passing two-wheeled vehicles without sidecars. That exception does not override the danger prohibition, continuous-line restrictions or the uncontrolled-crossing prohibition. None of these exceptions proves a manoeuvre safe. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §39

Do not overtake immediately before or on an uncontrolled pedestrian crossing, uncontrolled cycle passage or cycle crossing. Where parallel-lane passing is legally not classified as overtaking, the special crossing rule still requires a speed allowing an immediate stop for a person on the crossing or passage. Obey signs and continuous-line restrictions as well. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§11, 40–41

Overtaking signs and line information The prohibition and its end form a pair. For combined lines, identify the line nearest your lane. M20a warns of a coming centre-line or divider change; it is not an ordinary lane-change arrow.

Do not overtake motor vehicles other than two-wheeled mopeds and motorcycles without sidecars. Other overtaking safety rules still apply; the sign restriction continues to C28. Red and black cars side by side.
No overtaking. Red and black cars side by side.
The prohibition introduced by C27 ends. General overtaking restrictions still apply. Overtaking symbol crossed by diagonal black lines.
End of overtaking prohibition. Overtaking symbol crossed by diagonal black lines.
Line information
Crossing this line is unsuitable because of the traffic conditions. It may also warn of a continuous line ahead. Long white strokes with short gaps.
Warning line. Long white strokes with short gaps.
Continue the learning
Crossing restrictions apply according to the type of continuous line and the traffic rules. Do not invent an exception merely because the road appears clear. Single and double continuous white lines.
Continuous line. Single and double continuous white lines.
The continuous line governs a driver on its side of the marking. Do not treat the broken line on the other side as permission to change lanes. Broken white line beside a continuous line.
Broken line beside a continuous line. Broken white line beside a continuous line.
The continuous-line side restricts lane changes; the warning-line side indicates that crossing is unsuitable. Warning line beside a continuous line.
Warning line beside a continuous line. Warning line beside a continuous line.

Between opposing traffic lanes, this marking warns of a continuous centre line or physical separation ahead. It accompanies a centre line or warning line. Diagonal return arrow marking an approaching continuous centre line or physical separation.
Continuous centre line or divider ahead. Diagonal return arrow marking an approaching continuous centre line or physical separation.
Assess the whole passing path

Learning approach. Before moving, identify the full pass and return path, not merely the first gap. If completing it depends on another driver braking or on exceeding the limit, decline it. Small apparent time savings are not a reason to consume every margin. Trafikverket: speed and journey time
Following a slower vehicle towards a hidden bend. The visible straight does not establish a complete pass and return path. The depicted spacing is illustrative, not a recommended following distance.

Worked decision. A vehicle ahead travels slightly slower than you want. An approaching bend hides the final part of the pass. You stay behind at a useful distance. The first few clear metres do not establish a complete overtaking opportunity.
Check your understanding
Knowledge check. If the vehicle ahead accelerates during your pass, must you complete it at any cost?
Remember: Choosing not to pass is a complete decision.
Your goal: Plan motorway entry, lane choice, separation and exit, including a missed exit.

Requirements. Motorways are for eligible motor vehicles and combinations designed and permitted to travel at least 40 km/h; class I mopeds are excluded. This is an eligibility condition, not a command to maintain 40 km/h in a queue. Enter and leave through the designated starts, ends and access routes. Do not reverse, turn around, use the central divider or cross-connections, or stop outside designated parking/rest areas except as an unavoidable incident requires. The relevant restrictions also apply to expressways (motortrafikled) and their access routes. Traffic Regulation, chapter 9 §§1–2
Motorways and expressways Matched start/end pairs. The road regime does not override vehicle eligibility or the need to reduce speed for conditions. Motorway
Motorway rules begin here, unless the sign is advance information with a distance panel. White motorway symbol on green.
Motorway. White motorway symbol on green.
Continue the learning
The motorway ends here or at the distance indicated. Read the regime that follows. Motorway symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
End of motorway. Motorway symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
Expressway
Expressway rules apply. The sign may also appear as advance information with a distance panel. White car viewed from the front on green.
Expressway (motortrafikled). White car viewed from the front on green.
The expressway ends here or at the indicated distance. Expressway car symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
End of expressway. Expressway car symbol crossed by a red diagonal.
Continue the learning

In an acceleration lane, adapt speed to the traffic in the lane you intend to join and enter as soon as it can be done without danger or unnecessary obstruction. A safe joining movement is your responsibility; other drivers who notice the intended entry must adapt speed to facilitate it. Entry without an acceleration lane has a yielding rule. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§21, 23 and 43

Read the joining-road layout Independent joining and lane-configuration examples. A road retaining its own lane differs from an acceleration lane; visual resemblance alone does not establish priority.

The diagram shows a joining road with an acceleration lane. It does not give a joining driver an unconditional right to enter. A road joins from the right through an acceleration lane alongside one forward lane.
Joining road with acceleration lane. A road joins from the right through an acceleration lane alongside one forward lane.
The joining road continues in a separate lane. Read the actual lane layout and markings. A joining road becomes a separate forward lane beside two existing lanes.
Joining road with its own lane. A joining road becomes a separate forward lane beside two existing lanes.
Continue the learning
The arrows show the travel direction in each lane; any separation shown is part of the layout. One opposing lane on the left and two forward lanes on the right.
Lane directions along a road. One opposing lane on the left and two forward lanes on the right.
The arrows show the travel direction in each lane; any separation shown is part of the layout. One opposing lane and one forward lane with a divider between them.
Lane directions along a road. One opposing lane and one forward lane with a divider between them.

Normally use the rightmost lane intended for your vehicle. Keep a following distance suited to speed, visibility and conditions; do not copy a car ahead that is following too closely. Signs may establish a lower maximum than a road's general limit, and your vehicle combination may have a lower limit again. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§2 and 7, chapter 4 §20 and chapter 9 §1

For an exit, take the suitable lane in good time and enter the deceleration lane as soon as possible. If you miss the exit, continue to a permitted exit and re-plan; never reverse to recover it. A breakdown is dealt with in M10-L01, not by using the shoulder as a convenient place to check navigation.
Prepare the exit early Independent navigation examples, not a single continuous route connecting the printed destinations. The separation marker does not authorise a late lane change.
An exit is ahead at the indicated distance. Prepare the appropriate lane safely. Advance exit towards Ornäs, 500 m ahead, while route 50 continues ahead.
Advance exit information. Advance exit towards Ornäs, 500 m ahead, while route 50 continues ahead.
The exit begins at this sign. Do not make a late unsafe lane change to reach it. Exit sign pointing towards Mora via route 70 and towards Enköping.
Exit direction sign. Exit sign pointing towards Mora via route 70 and towards Enköping.
Use the lane or lanes beneath the relevant destination. Read any distance given for an upcoming exit. Overhead destinations: Boda on the left panel; Falun via route 50 on the right panel.
Overhead lane destinations. Overhead destinations: Boda on the left panel; Falun via route 50 on the right panel.
Continue the learning
Use the lane or lanes beneath the relevant destination. Read any distance given for an upcoming exit. Overhead lane information for Stockholm and Enköping via E18, with an exit in 500 m.
Overhead lane destinations. Overhead lane information for Stockholm and Enköping via E18, with an exit in 500 m.
This identifies the interchange number and may include an exit designation. Interchange number 75.
Interchange number. Interchange number 75.
This marks the split between the main carriageway and an exit with a deceleration lane. White upward chevrons on blue identify an exit separation.
Exit separation marker. White upward chevrons on blue identify an exit separation.
Adjust after faster traffic

After the motorway · Recheck your speed. After a long period at a steady motorway speed, your perception can adapt to that pace. On a slower road, the correct lower speed may feel unusually slow. This effect is often called speed adaptation or velocitation. Check the speedometer regularly to judge actual speed and adjust to the current limit and conditions. The feeling alone is not evidence that the speedometer is faulty. ODOT: speed perception and speedometer checks

Worked transition. After a long motorway trip, you leave onto a road signed 50 km/h. At 50, the car feels as if it is crawling. Confirm the speedometer reading, read the new road and retain a speed suited to its limit, visibility and hazards. Do not accelerate merely to recover the motorway's familiar feeling.
Plan entry and exit
Acceleration-lane detail: the teal car approaches traffic already on the main carriageway. Judge speed and a safe joining opportunity; this still image does not guarantee a usable gap.
Exit detail: plan the receiving lane early. If the necessary move cannot be made safely, continue to a permitted exit and re-plan; never reverse to recover the route.
Worked decision. Your exit sign appears while another vehicle occupies the lane you would need to cross. You do not force the move. You continue safely and tell your passenger the route will change.
Check your understanding

Knowledge check. (1) Does a posted motorway limit override a lower trailer-combination limit? (2) After prolonged motorway driving, the lower speed on your new road feels too slow. What explains that feeling, and what should guide your speed?
Remember: Prepare the next movement before the road makes it urgent.
Your goal: Interpret railway-crossing and roadworks information and approach changed lanes, queues and barriers safely.

Railway requirements. Approach with particular care and at a speed that allows a stop before the crossing. Do not enter when a train or tram is approaching, a red signal shows, an audible warning sounds, a barrier is lowering, lowered or rising, or you might have to stop on the tracks. Cross without unnecessary delay only when it is permitted and there is room beyond. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §7

Railway warnings and crossing controls Advance warnings, three/two/one countdown markers, crossbucks and active controls have different roles. Countdown boards do not specify fixed metre intervals. A still image does not reproduce flashing or sound. No crossing-ID number is invented. Advance warnings
A railway or tramway crossing fitted with barriers lies ahead. Follow its signals and barrier indications. Barrier pictogram inside a warning triangle.
Rail crossing with barriers. Barrier pictogram inside a warning triangle.
Continue the learning
Prepare for a railway crossing without barriers. The lack of barriers does not mean a train cannot approach. Locomotive inside a warning triangle.
Rail crossing without barriers. Locomotive inside a warning triangle.
A tramway crossing without barriers lies ahead. Tram inside a warning triangle.
Tram crossing without barriers. Tram inside a warning triangle.
Countdown to the crossing
The three markers divide the approach into thirds. They do not represent a universal fixed distance in metres. Three red diagonal bars on a yellow board.
Rail-crossing countdown. Three red diagonal bars on a yellow board.
Continue the learning
The three markers divide the approach into thirds. They do not represent a universal fixed distance in metres. Two red diagonal bars on a yellow board.
Rail-crossing countdown. Two red diagonal bars on a yellow board.
The three markers divide the approach into thirds. They do not represent a universal fixed distance in metres. One red diagonal bar on a yellow board.
Rail-crossing countdown. One red diagonal bar on a yellow board.
Crossing markers
The crossing is immediately ahead. The crossbuck arrangement distinguishes one track from multiple tracks. A single horizontal crossbuck, for one track.
Railway crossbuck. A single horizontal crossbuck, for one track.
Continue the learning
The crossing is immediately ahead. The crossbuck arrangement distinguishes one track from multiple tracks. An additional lower crossbuck element indicates multiple tracks.
Railway crossbuck. An additional lower crossbuck element indicates multiple tracks.
Signals, sound and barriers

Stop before the stop line or, without one, before the signal. The red lamps flash alternately; the illustration is a still representation. Two red signal lamps and a lower lamp within a downward-pointing signal backing; red flashing is represented by a still drawing.
Flashing red rail-crossing signal. Two red signal lamps and a lower lamp within a downward-pointing signal backing; red flashing is represented by a still drawing.

Do not enter the crossing while the audible warning is sounding. This graphic is only a sound icon, not a recording or a flashing-light instruction. Grey speaker icon with sound waves; no audio is supplied.
Rail-crossing audible warning. Grey speaker icon with sound waves; no audio is supplied.
Continue the learning
Do not enter while a barrier is lowering, lowered or rising. A raised barrier alone does not establish that crossing is safe. Red-and-yellow crossing barrier with a red lamp.
Rail-crossing barrier. Red-and-yellow crossing barrier with a red lamp.
This helps you identify a railway or tramway crossing. It is not itself a signal that permits entry. Blue board with white crossing shapes arranged vertically.
Rail-crossing visibility marker. Blue board with white crossing shapes arranged vertically.

Two different emergencies. Trafikverket says that if warnings begin while you are already crossing, continue out. If a functioning vehicle is trapped between the barriers, drive through the barrier to leave the tracks. If the vehicle has broken down on the tracks, evacuate everyone promptly, move well away and call 112. Give the crossing ID from the crossbuck sign if available without returning to danger. Do not stay on the tracks attempting a repair or pushing exercise. Trafikverket: level-crossing safety

Roadworks. Expect changed lanes, reduced speeds, workers and queues. Follow the current signs, signals and authorised guard directions; allow room around work areas and keep distance. A familiar road may now have a different usable path. Temporary guidance deserves attention before you reach the first barrier, not after you have entered the work area. Trafikverket: roadworks · Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §2 and chapter 3 §15

Roadworks and temporary guidance Independent recognition sets, not one verified work-zone layout. Keep directional, diagonal and horizontal markers distinct. Actual signs, signals and authorised directions govern the route. Warnings
Work is taking place along the road. Expect the usable route and traffic arrangements to change. Worker digging inside a warning triangle.
Roadworks. Worker digging inside a warning triangle.
The section marked by the roadworks warning ends here. Continue to follow any remaining restrictions. Roadworker pictogram crossed by a black diagonal band.
End of roadworks section. Roadworker pictogram crossed by a black diagonal band.
Prepare for a three-aspect traffic signal ahead; the warning itself is not a signal to proceed. Red, yellow and green lamps inside a warning triangle.
Traffic signals ahead. Red, yellow and green lamps inside a warning triangle.
Continue the learning
A hazard not covered by another warning sign is ahead. Read the supplementary description of the danger. Exclamation mark inside a warning triangle.
Other danger. Exclamation mark inside a warning triangle.
A queue may form on this stretch. Look far enough ahead to respond to slowing or stationary traffic. Queue of cars inside a warning triangle.
Queues ahead. Queue of cars inside a warning triangle.
Diversions and temporary routes
The ordinary road is temporarily closed. The diagram shows the diversion route. Orange diagram routes traffic around a closed part of the road.
Advance temporary diversion. Orange diagram routes traffic around a closed part of the road.
Continue the learning
Follow the indicated direction for the temporary diversion. Orange diversion arrow points right.
Temporary diversion direction. Orange diversion arrow points right.
A lane is temporarily closed and another lane in your direction is available. Prepare to move safely as indicated. One of two lanes closes; move into the other lane in the same direction.
Lane temporarily ends. One of two lanes closes; move into the other lane in the same direction.

A lane is temporarily closed with no other lane available in that travel direction. Read and follow the temporary routing rather than assuming an ordinary merge. An upward arrow meets a black closure block; a separate downward arrow marks opposing traffic.
Lane temporarily closed. An upward arrow meets a black closure block; a separate downward arrow marks opposing traffic.
Markers and physical guidance
Turn sharply in the direction of the yellow arrow or arrows. Temporary use, including roadworks, has a red background. Yellow chevron points left on blue.
Sharp-change direction marker. Yellow chevron points left on blue.
An obstruction restricts the road, which may be partly or fully closed. Temporary boards have a red background. Horizontal board divided into alternating blue and yellow vertical blocks.
Obstruction board. Horizontal board divided into alternating blue and yellow vertical blocks.

Pass on the side towards which the yellow diagonal stripes slope down. A temporary horizontal-striped version permits passage on either side. Diagonal yellow bands slope down towards the left on blue.
Side-obstruction marker. Diagonal yellow bands slope down towards the left on blue.
Continue the learning

Pass on the side towards which the yellow diagonal stripes slope down. A temporary horizontal-striped version permits passage on either side. Two red boards have yellow diagonal bands sloping down towards opposite outer sides.
Side-obstruction marker. Two red boards have yellow diagonal bands sloping down towards opposite outer sides.

Pass on the side towards which the yellow diagonal stripes slope down. A temporary horizontal-striped version permits passage on either side. Horizontal red and yellow bands; passage may be on either side.
Side-obstruction marker. Horizontal red and yellow bands; passage may be on either side.
Pass on a side indicated by the yellow illuminated arrow or arrows. The arrows may flash. Two illuminated yellow arrows point down to opposite sides.
Illuminated pass-side arrow. Two illuminated yellow arrows point down to opposite sides.
Continue the learning
A temporary obstruction restricts passage. Read the text identifying its cause. Temporary warning device reads Olycka: accident.
Temporary obstruction warning device. Temporary warning device reads Olycka: accident.
The barrier indicates that the road is wholly or partly closed to traffic. Red-and-yellow road barrier.
Road barrier. Red-and-yellow road barrier.
The crossed-out destination instruction is temporarily not valid. Read the replacement route guidance. Red cross over temporarily cancelled destination information.
Temporary cancellation of direction information. Red cross over temporarily cancelled destination information.
This makes the supporting sign or traffic device easier to see. It is not a separate destination or priority instruction. Blue and white bands around a signpost.
Signpost visibility marker. Blue and white bands around a signpost.
Authorised guard instructions
Stop if the guard faces you. A red lamp is used in darkness; an authorised stop sign marked Vakt may also be used. Guard faces approaching traffic and holds a red flag sideways.
Traffic guard — stop. Guard faces approaching traffic and holds a red flag sideways.
Proceed in the direction indicated by the guard's waving movement. A still image does not show the full gesture. Guard gestures to traffic; the complete movement is not reproduced in this still.
Traffic guard — proceed. Guard gestures to traffic; the complete movement is not reproduced in this still.
The guard identifier must be worn on the front and back. It identifies the role rather than giving a separate movement instruction. Garment identification panel bearing VAKT.
Traffic guard identifier. Garment identification panel bearing VAKT.
Check the space beyond the tracks

Railway-crossing detail: the tracks are unoccupied but traffic is queued beyond them. Check that the whole vehicle can clear the railway before entering. The crop does not depict every sign, signal or barrier.

Worked decision. Traffic beyond a railway crossing stops while the barriers are still raised. You wait before the crossing. An open barrier is not proof that there is space to get clear. Later, at roadworks, you read the temporary lane instructions instead of following the old route from memory.
The crossing ID is on the back of the crossbuck. Use it only if available without returning to danger; see the official level-crossing guide. Trafikverket: level-crossing safety
Read the temporary road

Roadworks detail: machinery and cones alter the usable road edge. The scene illustrates observation and space, not a complete approved traffic-management layout. Follow the actual signs, signals and authorised directions.
Check your understanding
Knowledge check. Your engine fails while the car is on the tracks. Is the priority to protect the car or to evacuate and call for help?
Remember: Never enter a space unless you can clear it, and protect people first when the situation changes.
Scenario: Your rural trip involves a slow vehicle, a motorway entry, temporary roadworks and a railway crossing with a queue beyond it.
Rural meeting detail: identify the visible road space and what an approaching vehicle changes.
Hidden-road detail: identify what remains out of view beyond the bend.
Use these rural details to describe what you can see and what remains uncertain.
Crossing and junction details
Ordinary rural-junction detail: assess possible joining traffic. This is separate from the motorway-entry detail shown later.
Railway detail: assess the queue and the available space beyond the tracks. No safe clearance is measured by the drawing.
Relate the details to the written trip. Explain what would change your decision.
Slower traffic and motorway entry
Slower-vehicle detail for the written trip: describe the observations and space needed before deciding whether to pass.
Motorway-entry detail for the written trip: describe how you would assess speed and traffic before joining.
Relate the details to the written trip. Explain what would change your decision.
Bring the journey together
Roadworks detail for the written trip: identify the information you need about the temporary route. No path is selected for you.
Identify where you might have to wait or change the route.
Keep a practice record
Record one situation in which impatience could change your judgement. Explain the risk and identify a practice or planning action that preserves your margin. Syllabus self-assessment, chapter 3 §3
